question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>17</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> completely vapourises at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>33</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>42</mn><mo> </mo><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> bar pressure and the enthalpy change in the process is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>23</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The enthalpy change for the vapourisation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>85</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>NH</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> under the same conditions is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kJ</mi></math>.

solution.text:
17.0 g of NH3 = 1717 = 1 mole and the enthalpy change = 23.4 kJ mol-1.

 85 g of NH3 = 8517 = 5 moles enthalpy change under the same conditions will be = 23.4×5=117 kJ.
